# R1.5 - Visits per patient and what the first-visit restriction discards

*Generated by `r1_05_r2_01_repeat_visits.R` on 2026-08-18. All figures are computed on the 417,723 eligible visits (rows with missing acuity, age or race removed), before the first-visit restriction, unless stated otherwise.*

## Verdict

The reviewer is right that the restriction discards a large share of the data: 216,617 of the 417,723 eligible visits (51.9%) are repeat presentations that never enter the published analysis, leaving 201,106 index visits, one per patient. ED use in MIMIC-IV-ED is heavily concentrated - the median patient contributes a single visit, but the mean is 2.08 and one patient attended 320 times, and the top 10% of patients by visit count account for 40.2% of all eligible visits. Frequent attenders are therefore genuinely under-represented at the *visit* level, exactly as the reviewer says, and they are not a random subset of patients: compared with single-visit patients they are older (median age 53 vs 46 years), more often female (55.0% vs 52.9%), and more often Black (21.6% vs 13.0%) or Hispanic/Latino (8.2% vs 5.6%).
What does not follow is a material distortion of the headline estimate. The index visits of repeat attenders are flagged by at least one algorithm at almost the same rate as those of single-visit patients (49.0% vs 50.5%), because the individual algorithms move in opposite directions: Diagnosis is higher in repeat attenders (36.4% vs 32.6%) while Resources (20.4% vs 25.8%) and Triage-Acuity (6.9% vs 8.3%) are lower, and these largely cancel.
The companion sensitivity analysis (`r2_01_sensitivity_all_visits.md`) confirms this directly: re-running all three algorithms on every eligible visit moves no headline figure by more than 2.2 percentage points, and none of the paper's three conclusions changes.
The restriction is therefore best described in the manuscript as a deliberate choice of the *patient* rather than the *visit* as the unit of analysis, which keeps observations independent, rather than as a source of bias.

## 1. What the restriction discards

| Quantity | N | % of eligible visits |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Eligible visits | 417,723 | 100.0 |
| First visits retained (published sample) | 201,106 | 48.1 |
| **Repeat visits discarded** | **216,617** | **51.9** |

Of the 424,707 rows in the source file, 6,984 are dropped for missing acuity, age or race before any of this, leaving the 417,723 eligible visits used throughout.

## 2. Distribution of visits per patient

Across 201,106 patients contributing 417,723 eligible visits:

| Statistic | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Median visits per patient | 1 (IQR 1-2) |
| Mean visits per patient | 2.08 |
| Maximum visits by a single patient | 320 |

| Visits per patient | Patients (N) | Patients (%) | Visits (N) | Visits (%) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 132,184 | 65.7 | 132,184 | 31.6 |
| 2 | 32,131 | 16.0 | 64,262 | 15.4 |
| 3 | 13,511 | 6.7 | 40,533 | 9.7 |
| 4-5 | 11,581 | 5.8 | 50,615 | 12.1 |
| 6-10 | 8,027 | 4.0 | 59,233 | 14.2 |
| 11-20 | 2,746 | 1.4 | 38,304 | 9.2 |
| 21+ | 926 | 0.5 | 32,592 | 7.8 |

Two thirds of patients (65.7%) attend exactly once, but those single attendances make up only 31.6% of eligible visits. Conversely the 5.8% of patients attending six or more times contribute 31.2% of all visits.

## 3. Concentration among frequent attenders

This is the quantitative form of the reviewer's point.

| Patient group (ranked by visit count) | Patients (N) | Visit-count threshold | Visits contributed (N) | Share of all eligible visits (%) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Top 1% | 2,012 | >= 14 | 50,798 | 12.2 |
| Top 5% | 10,056 | >= 6 | 120,271 | 28.8 |
| Top 10% | 20,111 | >= 4 | 168,068 | 40.2 |

The heaviest-attending 1% of patients (2,012 people, each with 14 or more eligible visits) account for 12.2% of all eligible ED visits. Under the first-visit design each of them contributes exactly one row, the same weight as a patient who attended once.

*Patients are ranked by visit count in descending order and the top k taken, where k is the ceiling of the stated percentage of patients. Ties at the boundary are broken arbitrarily, so the visit-count threshold is reported to make each cut-off transparent.*

## 4. Are the retained index visits representative?

Patients with exactly one eligible visit compared with patients who had two or more, using each patient's **first** visit - which for single-visit patients is their only visit. This is the relevant comparison, because the published sample consists exactly of these index visits.

| Characteristic | Single-visit patients | Repeat-visit patients (2+) | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Patients (N) | 132,184 | 68,922 | - |
| Age, median (years) | 46 | 53 | +7 |
| Age, mean (years) | 47.4 | 52.6 | +5.2 |
| Female (%) | 52.9 | 55.0 | +2.1 |

Self-reported race, collapsed exactly as in Table 1 of the paper:

| Race | Single-visit patients (%) | Repeat-visit patients (%) | Difference (pp) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| White | 64.3 | 58.1 | -6.1 |
| Black | 13.0 | 21.6 | +8.6 |
| Hispanic/Latino | 5.6 | 8.2 | +2.6 |
| Asian | 6.1 | 4.6 | -1.5 |
| Other | 11.1 | 7.5 | -3.6 |

Flag rate at the index visit, by algorithm:

| Algorithm | Single-visit patients (%) | Repeat-visit patients (%) | Difference (pp) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Diagnosis | 32.6 | 36.4 | +3.9 |
| Resources | 25.8 | 20.4 | -5.3 |
| Triage-Acuity | 8.3 | 6.9 | -1.4 |
| **Any of the three** | **50.5** | **49.0** | **-1.5** |

Repeat attenders differ demographically and their index visit is somewhat more likely to be flagged by the Diagnosis algorithm (36.4% vs 32.6%), but it is *less* likely to be flagged by Resources (20.4% vs 25.8%) and Triage-Acuity (6.9% vs 8.3%). The net effect on the headline "flagged by at least one algorithm" figure is -1.5 percentage points. This offsetting is the mechanism behind the near-identical first-visit and all-visit estimates reported in the sensitivity analysis.
